<h2 id="create-font-w"><code>CreateFontW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func CreateFontW(
    height: int32,
    width: int32,
    escapement: int32,
    orientation: int32,
    weight: int32,
    italic: uint32,
    underline: uint32,
    strikeOut: uint32,
    charSet: uint32,
    outPrecision: uint32,
    clipPrecision: uint32,
    quality: uint32,
    pitchAndFamily: uint32,
    faceName: *char16
) -> *var opaque
```

Creates a logical font, which the mapper matches to the closest installed font when it is selected.
A negative height asks for that many pixels of character height without the internal leading, which is how a
point size is given: `-(points * dpi / 72)`.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-createfontw](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-createfontw)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Gdi.rux#L78)

**Parameters**

| Name             | Type      | Description                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `height`         | `int32`   | the character height in pixels, negative for the character height without the leading                     |
| `width`          | `int32`   | the average character width, or zero to derive it from the height                                         |
| `escapement`     | `int32`   | the angle of the text line, in tenths of a degree                                                         |
| `orientation`    | `int32`   | the angle of each character, in tenths of a degree                                                        |
| `weight`         | `int32`   | the weight, such as [`FW_NORMAL`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#fw-normal)                                        |
| `italic`         | `uint32`  | non-zero for italic                                                                                       |
| `underline`      | `uint32`  | non-zero for underlined                                                                                   |
| `strikeOut`      | `uint32`  | non-zero for struck out                                                                                   |
| `charSet`        | `uint32`  | the character set, usually [`DEFAULT_CHARSET`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#default-charset)                     |
| `outPrecision`   | `uint32`  | how closely the font must match, usually [`OUT_DEFAULT_PRECIS`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#out-default-precis) |
| `clipPrecision`  | `uint32`  | how characters are clipped, usually [`CLIP_DEFAULT_PRECIS`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#clip-default-precis)    |
| `quality`        | `uint32`  | how it is smoothed, such as [`CLEARTYPE_QUALITY`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#cleartype-quality)                |
| `pitchAndFamily` | `uint32`  | the pitch and family, usually [`DEFAULT_PITCH`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#default-pitch)                      |
| `faceName`       | `*char16` | the NUL-terminated UTF-16 face name, such as `Segoe UI`                                                   |

**Returns**: the font, which the caller deletes with [`DeleteObject`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#delete-object), or null on failure

<h2 id="delete-object"><code>DeleteObject</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func DeleteObject(object: *var opaque) -> bool32
```

Deletes a GDI object such as a font, giving back what the system holds for it.
An object still selected into a device context is not deleted, and the call fails.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-deleteobject](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-deleteobject)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Gdi.rux#L101)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type          | Description          |
| -------- | ------------- | -------------------- |
| `object` | `*var opaque` | the object to delete |

**Returns**: non-zero on success, and zero when the handle is not valid or the object is still selected

<h2 id="select-object"><code>SelectObject</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func SelectObject(
    deviceContext: *var opaque,
    object: *var opaque
) -> *var opaque
```

Selects a font or another GDI object into a device context, replacing the one of the same kind.
The object replaced is returned so it can be selected back before the context is given up.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-selectobject](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-selectobject)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Gdi.rux#L110)

**Parameters**

| Name            | Type          | Description          |
| --------------- | ------------- | -------------------- |
| `deviceContext` | `*var opaque` | the device context   |
| `object`        | `*var opaque` | the object to select |

**Returns**: the object it replaced, or null on failure

<h2 id="set-bk-mode"><code>SetBkMode</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func SetBkMode(
    deviceContext: *var opaque,
    mode: int32
) -> int32
```

Sets whether text is drawn on a filled cell or straight onto what is already there.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-setbkmode](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-setbkmode)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Gdi.rux#L118)

**Parameters**

| Name            | Type          | Description                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deviceContext` | `*var opaque` | the device context                                                                             |
| `mode`          | `int32`       | [`TRANSPARENT`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#transparent) or [`OPAQUE`](/docs/api/windows/gdi#opaque) |

**Returns**: the mode before the call, or zero on failure

Sets the color text is drawn in.

| Name            | Type          | Description                                                                                         |
| --------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deviceContext` | `*var opaque` | the device context                                                                                  |
| `color`         | `uint32`      | the color as `0x00BBGGRR`, such as one from [`GetSysColor`](/docs/api/windows/window#get-sys-color) |

<h2 id="text-out-w"><code>TextOutW</code></h2>

```rux
pub extern func TextOutW(
    deviceContext: *var opaque,
    x: int32,
    y: int32,
    text: *char16,
    count: int32
) -> bool32
```

Draws a run of UTF-16 text with its top-left corner at a point, in the selected font and text color.
The run is counted rather than NUL-terminated, and is not wrapped or clipped to the window.

**See also**: [https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-textoutw](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-textoutw)

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Windows/Src/Gdi.rux#L138)

**Parameters**

| Name            | Type          | Description              |
| --------------- | ------------- | ------------------------ |
| `deviceContext` | `*var opaque` | the device context       |
| `x`             | `int32`       | the left edge, in pixels |
| `y`             | `int32`       | the top edge, in pixels  |
| `text`          | `*char16`     | the UTF-16 units to draw |
| `count`         | `int32`       | how many units to draw   |

**Returns**: non-zero on success, and zero on failure
